Let $\mathscr C$ be a [[Definition:Non-Empty Set|non-empty]] [[Definition:Set|set]] of [[Definition:Subset|subsets]] of $S$.
:$\mathscr C$ is the [[Definition:Set|set]] of [[Definition:Circuit (Matroid)|circuits]] of a [[Definition:Matroid|matroid]] on $S$
From [[Equivalence of Definitions of Matroid Circuit Axioms]] it is sufficient to show:

:$(\text a)\quad$if $\mathscr C$ is the [[Definition:Set|set]] of [[Definition:Circuit (Matroid)|circuits]] of a [[Definition:Matroid|matroid]] then $\mathscr C$ satisfies [[Axiom:Circuit Axioms (Matroid)/Formulation 1|circuit axioms (formulation 1)]]

:$(\text b)\quad$if $\mathscr C$ satisfies [[Axiom:Circuit Axioms (Matroid)/Formulation 2|circuit axioms (formulation 2)]] then $\mathscr C$ is the [[Definition:Set|set]] of [[Definition:Circuit (Matroid)|circuits]] of a [[Definition:Matroid|matroid]]
=== [[Circuits of Matroid iff Matroid Circuit Axioms/Circuits of Matroid implies Formulation 1|Circuits of Matroids implies Formulation 1]] ===
Let $\mathscr C$ be the [[Definition:Set|set]] of [[Definition:Circuit (Matroid)|circuits]] of a [[Definition:Matroid|matroid]] $M = \struct{S, \mathscr I}$ on $S$
It is shown that $\mathscr C$ satisfies the [[Axiom:Circuit Axioms (Matroid)/Formulation 1|circuit axioms (formulation 1)]]:
| mr= C_1 \ne C_2 \land z \in C_1 \cap C_2 \implies \exists C_3 \in \mathscr C : C_3 \subseteq \paren {C_1 \cup C_2} \setminus \set z
:for all $C \in \mathscr C: C$ is a [[Definition:Dependent Subset (Matroid)|dependent subset]]
By definition of a [[Definition:Dependent Subset (Matroid)|dependent subset]]:
It follows that $\mathscr C$ satisfies [[Axiom:Circuit Axioms (Matroid)/Formulation 1|circuit axiom $(\text C 1)$]].

It follows that $\mathscr C$ satisfies [[Axiom:Circuit Axioms (Matroid)/Formulation 1|circuit axiom $(\text C 2)$]].
Let $\rho$ denote the [[Definition:Rank Function (Matroid)|rank function]] of the [[Definition:Matroid|matroid]] $M$.

From [[Proper Subset of Matroid Circuit is Independent]]:

It follows that $\mathscr C$ satisfies [[Axiom:Circuit Axioms (Matroid)/Formulation 1|circuit axiom $(\text C 3)$]].{{qed|lemma}}
=== [[Circuits of Matroid iff Matroid Circuit Axioms/Formulation 2 implies Circuits of Matroid|Formulation 2 implies Circuits of Matroid]] ===

Let $\mathscr C$ be a [[Definition:Non-Empty Set|non-empty]] [[Definition:Set|set]] of [[Definition:Subset|subsets]] of $S$ that satisfies the [[Axiom:Circuit Axioms (Matroid)/Formulation 2|circuit axioms (formulation 2)]]:
| mr = C_1 \ne C_2 \land z \in C_1 \cap C_2 \land w \in C_1 \setminus C_2 \implies \exists C_3 \in \mathscr C : w \in C_3 \subseteq \paren {C_1 \cup C_2} \setminus \set z
We will define a [[Definition:Mapping|mapping]] $\rho$ associated with $\mathscr C$.

It will be shown that $\rho$ is the [[Definition:Rank Function (Matroid)|rank function]] of a [[Definition:Matroid|matroid]] $M$ which has $\mathscr C$ as the set of [[Definition:Circuit (Matroid)|circuits]].

For any [[Definition:Ordered Tuple|ordered tuple]] $\tuple{x_1, \ldots, x_q}$ of [[Definition:Element|elements]] of $S$, let $\map \theta {x_1, \ldots, x_q}$ be the [[Definition:Ordered Tuple|ordered tuple]] defined by:

:$\forall i \in \set{1, \ldots, q} : \map \theta {x_1, \ldots, x_q}_i = \begin{cases} 0 & : \exists C \in \mathscr C : x_i \in C \subseteq \set{x_1, \ldots, x_i}\\ 1 & : \text {otherwise}  \end{cases}$
Let $t$ be the [[Definition:Mapping|mapping]] from the [[Definition:Set|set]] of [[Definition:Ordered Tuple|ordered tuple]] of $S$ defined  by:
==== [[Circuits of Matroid iff Matroid Circuit Axioms/Lemma 1|Lemma 1]] ====
Let $\tuple{x_1, \ldots, x_q}$ be any [[Definition:Ordered Tuple|ordered tuple]] of [[Definition:Element|elements]] of $S$.
Let $\rho : \powerset S \to \Z$ be the [[Definition:Mapping|mapping]] defined by:
::$\map \rho A = \begin{cases} 0 & : \text{if } A = \O \\ \map t {x_1, \ldots, x_q } & : \text{if } A = \set{x_1, \ldots, x_q} \end{cases}$
From [[Circuits of Matroid iff Matroid Circuit Axioms/Lemma 1|Lemma 1]]:
We now show that $\rho$ satisfies the [[Axiom:Rank Axioms (Matroid)/Definition 1|rank function axioms]]:
| q = \forall X \in \powerset S \land y, z \in S
| mr= \map \rho {X \cup \set y} = \map \rho {X \cup \set z} = \map \rho X \implies \map \rho {X \cup \set y \cup \set z} = \map \rho X
| r = \map t {\tuple{x_1, \dots, x_q, y} } - \map t {\tuple{x_1, \dots, x_q} }
{{eqn | r = \begin{cases} 0 & : \exists C \in \mathscr C : y \in C \subseteq \set{x_1, \ldots, x_q, y}\\ 1 & : \text {otherwise} \end{cases}
| c = Adding $\map \rho X$ to all terms
==== [[Circuits of Matroid iff Matroid Circuit Axioms/Lemma 2|Lemma 2]] ====
:$\map \rho {X \cup \set y} = \map \rho X$ {{iff}} $\exists C \in \mathscr C : y \in C \subseteq X \cup \set y${{qed|lemma}}
From [[Circuits of Matroid iff Matroid Circuit Axioms/Lemma 2|Lemma 2]]:
:$\exists C_z \in \mathscr C : z \in C_z \subseteq X \cup \set{z} \subseteq X \cup \set{y,z}$
From [[Circuits of Matroid iff Matroid Circuit Axioms/Lemma 2|Lemma 2]]:
From [[Matroid Rank Function Iff Matroid Rank Axioms]]:
:$\rho$ is the [[Definition:Rank Function (Matroid)|rank function]] of a [[Definition:Matroid|matroid]] $M = \struct{S, \mathscr I}$ on $S$
==== [[Circuits of Matroid iff Matroid Circuit Axioms/Lemma 3|Lemma 3]] ====
:$\mathscr C$ is the set of [[Definition:Circuit (Matroid)|circuits]] of $M$.{{qed}}
